Definition: from G213; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence:--boasting, pride.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times it is the pride that talks. James hears men boasting in their plans, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain, and calls all such rejoicing evil. John names the pride of life beside the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes, and says it is not of the Father but of the world.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for bragging carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that planning tomorrow as if God had no say in it is not confidence but pride.
RelatedPeople: James, Brother of Jesus; John the Apostle
